speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I see you have a pruritic rash on both upper arms. To understand what this is, have you noticed any new soaps, detergents, or plants like poison ivy you've been exposed to recently? Also, does the itching occur at night more than during the day?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies (crusted or typical). The chronic duration, bilateral distribution, lack of response to standard care, and absence of obvious allergic triggers strongly suggest a mite infestation. Please confirm if you have seen burrows or excoriations on your wrists, finger webs, or waistline, and have any household members developed similar symptoms? REQUEST TEST: Microscopic skin scraping for mites, eggs, or feces; REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up photos of wrist and web spaces.
